mealie-mcp.name: get_recipes
mealie-mcp.description:
Provides a paginated list of recipes with optional filtering.

IMPORTANT: When filtering by tags or categories, you MUST use slugs or UUIDs, NOT display names!
- ✅ Correct: tags=["quick-meals", "vegetarian"]
- ❌ Wrong: tags=["Quick Meals", "Vegetarian"]

Use get_tags() or get_categories() first to find the correct slugs.

Args:
    search: Filters recipes by name or description.
    page: Page number for pagination.
    per_page: Number of items per page.
    categories: Filter by category SLUGS (e.g., ["breakfast", "dinner"]).
    tags: Filter by tag SLUGS or UUIDs (e.g., ["quick", "healthy"]).
    require_all_tags: If True, recipe must have ALL specified tags (AND). Default False (OR).
    require_all_categories: If True, recipe must have ALL specified categories (AND).

Returns:
    Dict[str, Any]: Recipe summaries with details like ID, name, description, and image information.

mealie-mcp.name: get_recipe_detailed

mealie-mcp.description:
Retrieve a concise version of a specific recipe by its slug identifier. Use this when you only

mealie-mcp.name: create_recipe
mealie-mcp.description:
Create a new recipe.

Ingredients and instructions each accept either a plain string or a
structured object:

- An ingredient string (e.g. "200 g basmati rice") is resolved by
  Mealie's natural-language parser into quantity/unit/food.
- An ingredient object can set quantity, note, title, an existing
  Mealie unit/food (by id and name), and a referenceId for step links.
- An instruction string is the step text; an instruction object can
  also carry a title and ingredientReferences for cook-mode highlights.

Args:
    name: The name of the new recipe to be created.
    ingredients: Ingredient strings and/or structured ingredient objects.
    instructions: Instruction strings and/or structured instruction objects.

Returns:
    Dict[str, Any]: The created recipe details.

RecipeIngredientInput.description:
Structured ingredient accepted by the create/update recipe tools.

Pass a plain string instead of this object to let Mealie's
natural-language parser resolve the quantity, unit, and food.

referenceId.description: Id used to link instruction steps to this ingredient. Mealie stores it as a UUID v4; any string is accepted and non-v4 values are converted to a stable UUID v4 server-side. Reuse the same value on the step's ingredientReferences to keep the link.
referenceId.title: Referenceid

unit.description: Existing Mealie unit object. Mealie requires both the id and the name, e.g. {"id": "<uuid>", "name": "gram"}.
unit.title: Unit

food.description: Existing Mealie food object. Mealie requires both the id and the name, e.g. {"id": "<uuid>", "name": "rice"}.
food.title: Food

note.description: Free-text qualifier shown after the food, e.g. "Basmati".
note.title: Note

title.description: Section heading rendered above this ingredient.
title.title: Title

RecipeIngredientInput.title: RecipeIngredientInput

RecipeInstructionInput.description:
Structured preparation step accepted by the create/update recipe tools.

Pass a plain string instead of this object for a step that has no title
and no ingredient links.

text.description: The instruction text for this step.
text.title: Text

title.description: Optional heading for this step or section.
title.title: Title

ingredientReferences.description: referenceIds of the ingredients used in this step; must match the referenceId set on those ingredients (Mealie requires UUID v4 here; non-v4 values are converted to a stable UUID v4 server-side). Enables Mealie's cook-mode highlighting.
ingredientReferences.title: Ingredientreferences

mealie-mcp.name: import_recipe_from_url
mealie-mcp.description:
Import a recipe into Mealie by scraping a URL.

Uses Mealie's server-side scraper (the `recipe-scrapers` library), which
has built-in adapters for many recipe sites and falls back to
JSON-LD/Schema.org parsing for sites without a dedicated adapter.
Coverage varies by Mealie version; URLs the scraper can't parse return
a 400 from Mealie.

The created recipe is fetched and returned so the caller can verify the
scrape result. Some sources (notably paywalled URLs that redirect) can
cause the scraper to land on the wrong page and silently return the
wrong recipe — always confirm the returned `name` matches what was
requested.

Args:
    url: Source URL of the recipe to import.
    include_tags: If True, import tags Mealie extracts from the source.
        Defaults to False.

Returns:
    Dict[str, Any]: The created recipe, including slug, name,
    ingredients, and instructions.

mealie-mcp.name: create_recipe_full
mealie-mcp.description:
Create a recipe and populate all of its content in one call.

Use this instead of create_recipe when you already have complete
recipe data (description, timing, servings, source URL, ingredients,
steps, and optionally an image URL). It creates the recipe, fills in
every provided field, and sets the image by scraping image_url when
given.

Ingredients and instructions accept the same flat-string or structured
forms as create_recipe.

Args:
    name: The name of the new recipe.
    description: Recipe description.
    org_url: Source URL for the recipe (shown as a link in the Mealie UI).
    total_time: Total time as free text, e.g. "35 min" or ISO-8601 "PT35M".
    prep_time: Preparation time, same format as total_time.
    cook_time: Cooking time, same format as total_time.
    perform_time: Hands-on/active time, same format as total_time.
    recipe_yield: Yield as free text, e.g. "4 Portionen".
    servings: Number of servings (numeric).
    image_url: URL of an image to scrape and set as the recipe image.
    ingredients: Ingredient strings and/or structured ingredient objects.
    instructions: Instruction strings and/or structured instruction objects.
    tags: Existing Mealie tags (id+name) to assign; look up with get_tags.
    tools: Existing Mealie tools (id+name) to assign; look up with get_tools.

Returns:
    Dict[str, Any]: The created recipe details.

Reference to an existing Mealie tag, category, or tool.

both the id and the name.

name.description: Display name of the existing organizer.

slug.description: Optional slug; Mealie derives it when omitted.

mealie-mcp.name: get_foods
mealie-mcp.description:
List the household's foods, optionally filtered by a search term.

Use this to resolve an existing Mealie food id+name before building a
structured ingredient, instead of hardcoding UUIDs. The Mealie search is
token-based; do client-side matching against the returned items if you
need fuzzy matching (e.g. "Basmatireis" -> "Reis").

Args:
    search: Search term to filter foods by name/alias.
    page: Page number to retrieve.
    per_page: Number of items per page.

Returns:
    Dict[str, Any]: Foods (under "items") with pagination information.

mealie-mcp.name: set_recipe_image_from_url
mealie-mcp.description:
Set a recipe's image by scraping from a URL — verified.

After Mealie processes the request this tool re-reads the recipe to
confirm the image field actually updated to a non-empty value. If it
didn't (most common cause: source URL returned 4xx anti-bot), the
call raises with a clear next-step suggestion (different URL,
og:image from the recipe's source page, or upload_recipe_image_file
with a local file).

Args:
    slug: The unique text identifier for the recipe.
    image_url: URL of the image to fetch.

Returns:
    On success: {"success": True, "slug": ..., "image_id": ..., "url_used": ...}
    On verified failure: raises with a helpful message naming the URL.

mealie-mcp.name: set_recipe_org_url
mealie-mcp.description:
Set a recipe's original source URL — verified.

Mealie's `orgURL` field is shown as a clickable "view original
recipe" link in the UI. Call this after create_recipe (or use
create_recipe_full's org_url parameter to set it in one step) to
record where a recipe came from. Do NOT put the URL in the
description field — that's not link-clickable and clutters prose
with a raw URL.

Args:
    slug: The unique text identifier for the recipe.
    org_url: The recipe's original source URL.

Returns:
    On success: {"success": True, "slug": ..., "org_url": ...}
    On verified failure: raises with a message naming the recipe.

rpg-dice-mcp.name: roll
rpg-dice-mcp.description: Roll a generic dice expression (NdM±K). Use this for any non-system-specific roll: 2d6+1, 1d20, 3d8-2, d12. For The One Ring tests, prefer roll_tor_check which encodes the system rules.

rpg-dice-mcp.name: roll_tor_check
rpg-dice-mcp.description: Resolve a The One Ring check. Rolls the Feat die (d12) plus skill_rating × Success dice (d6), interprets Eye/Gandalf special faces, applies weariness if set, and reports succeeds/margin against the TN. The Loremaster calls this for NPC/Loremaster-side rolls (per the dice-resolution skill). Player-side rolls are physical — the Loremaster only frames them.

format.description: Optional rendering style. When set, the response includes a `formatted` field with the result as a display-ready string. Values: "html_tor" (HTML with .fdie/.sdie span classes for the homelab CSS theme — use this from the OWUI Loremaster surface and the dice-roller web app), "plain" (no markup, for terminals/logs), "markdown" (emoji + bold for Discord/Slack), or "none" (default — no formatted field). The structured fields (feat_die, success_dice, etc.) are always present regardless of format.

miserable.description: When true, an Eye result sets MiserableEye in the response for Hope/Shadow bookkeeping.

skill_rating.description: Rating of the relevant skill or attribute (>= 0). Determines Success dice count.

target_number.description: TN to meet or beat for success.

weariness.description: When true, Success die rolls of 1-3 are treated as 0.

rpg-dice-mcp.name: roll_tor_combat
rpg-dice-mcp.description: Resolve a TOR combat attack roll. Thin wrapper over roll_tor_check using combat-flavored field names (attacker_skill / defender_tn). In TOR Strider Mode the player rolls most combat checks; use this when the Loremaster genuinely needs to roll for an NPC's offensive action.

attacker_skill.description: Rating of the attacker's weapon skill (Sword, Spear, Bow, etc.). Success dice count.

format.description: Optional rendering style. When set, the response includes a `formatted` field with the result as a display-ready string. Values: "html_tor" (HTML with .fdie/.sdie span classes for the homelab CSS theme — use this from the OWUI Loremaster surface and the dice-roller web app), "plain" (no markup, for terminals/logs), "markdown" (emoji + bold for Discord/Slack), or "none" (default — no formatted field). The structured fields (feat_die, success_dice, etc.) are always present regardless of format.

miserable.description: When true, Eye results trigger MiserableEye flag.

weariness.description: When true, attacker's Success dice 1-3 count as 0.

rpg-dice-mcp.name: tor_adjudicate
rpg-dice-mcp.description: Rule on HOW a One Ring situation resolves, before any dice are thrown. Returns who rolls, the Target Number, the Success dice count, and the hero's derived Weary/Miserable state — each computed from the Core Rules rather than recalled. Call this FIRST for any mechanical question or contested action, then roll_tor_check with the returned target_number and success_dice. Do not state a TN, a dice count, or who rolls without calling this: those values are computed here and are not reliably remembered.

action.description: What is being resolved. hero_skill/hero_attack/protection_test are rolled by the player; adversary_attack/eye_awareness/hidden_hazard/npc_wits are rolled by the Loremaster.

armour_protection.description: PROTECTION value of the armour worn (protection_test dice).

endurance.description: Hero's CURRENT Endurance. With load, derives Weary.

hope.description: Hero's current Hope. With shadow, derives Miserable.

hope_spent.description: Hope points the player spends on this roll. At most 1 is legal.

load.description: Hero's Load score. Weary when Endurance <= Load.

shadow.description: Hero's current Shadow. Miserable when Hope <= Shadow.

skill_rating.description: Rating of the relevant skill, attribute, or WEAPON PROFICIENCY. "Sword rating 4" goes here. Sets the Success dice count.

strength.description: The hero's STRENGTH ATTRIBUTE (a 1-8 character stat, not a weapon rating). REQUIRED for hero_attack: the TN is (20 - STRENGTH) + the target's Parry.

target_number.description: Explicit TN, when the situation does not derive one.

target_parry.description: Parry rating of the enemy being attacked (hero_attack).

weapon_injury.description: protection_test ONLY: the Injury rating of the ADVERSARY's weapon, used as that test's TN. Not used for hero_attack, and not the hero's weapon proficiency (that is skill_rating).

wiki-mcp.name: wiki_audit
wiki-mcp.description: Audit the link-graph health of a domain. Returns hubs (most-linked-to pages), orphans (pages no one links to), and dangling wikilink targets that don't resolve to any existing page in any domain. Reports state; does NOT mutate. Call this at the end of a writing session — orphans are entities to weave in, dangling targets are entities to write next (or links to remove if the target was speculative).

domain.description: Domain to audit (e.g., fiction, one-ring, homelab).

wiki-mcp.name: wiki_import
wiki-mcp.description:
Import a canonical Middle-earth place into the wiki ON DEMAND from Tolkien Gateway. Use this when wiki_search(domain="one-ring", query=<place>) returns no hits for what looks like a real Tolkien place: call wiki_import with the term, then call wiki_lookup with the returned slug. 

Returns one of five statuses (read the `status` field and act accordingly):
  - `imported`: page added AND visible locally; call wiki_lookup(domain="one-ring", slug=<returned slug>) right away.
  - `imported_pending`: page added to the remote wiki but the local cache has not synced yet. Wait ~30s and call wiki_lookup. Do NOT name canonical geography for this place until the lookup succeeds.
  - `not_found`: Tolkien Gateway has no page for this term. The place is non-canonical OR misspelled. DO NOT proceed to name distances/directions; ask the player to clarify or describe vaguely.
  - `disambiguation`: multiple TG pages match. Ask the player which they meant, then re-call wiki_import.
  - `error`: import pipeline failed (network/script). Describe the journey vaguely without naming canonical geography.

DO NOT call this tool for the same term twice in the same session — check your tool history first. DO NOT call this for places that are obviously player-invented (the player's hometown, etc.).

domain.description: Wiki domain to write into. Default: "one-ring".

slug.description: Optional local slug override. Default: slugify(term).

term.description: Tolkien Gateway page name (e.g. "Dunland", "Lonely Mountain", "Weathertop"). Match TG's capitalization when possible.

type.description: Wiki entry type. Default: "entity". One of: entity, concept, source, synthesis.

wiki-mcp.name: wiki_list_domains
wiki-mcp.description: List all domains in the wiki (one-ring, homelab, fiction, etc.). Useful when the caller doesn't know which domain a topic lives in.

wiki-mcp.name: wiki_lookup
wiki-mcp.description: Fetch a single wiki page by its (domain, slug). Returns the page's frontmatter, body, and metadata. Use this when you know the exact page you need. For finding pages by content/keywords, use wiki_search instead.

wiki-mcp.name: wiki_neighbors
wiki-mcp.description: Return all pages directly linked from the given page via [[wikilink]] syntax. Handles in-domain, cross-section, and cross-domain links. Only RESOLVED links appear (broken wikilinks are silently skipped).

wiki-mcp.name: wiki_search
wiki-mcp.description: Search a domain's wiki pages by keyword. Matches against aliases, tags, slug, and body — case-insensitive. Returns pages sorted by relevance (alias/tag hits > slug hits > body hits). Returns the metadata of each hit; call wiki_lookup to retrieve full page bodies.

wiki-mcp.name: wiki_write
wiki-mcp.description: Create or overwrite a wiki page. Writes to the local mount; a git-sync sidecar in the deploy pod commits + pushes on a separate schedule. WILL REFUSE: writes under raw/ (immutable per AGENTS.md), invalid domain/slug (must be lowercase-kebab), or invalid type (must be entities/concepts/sources/syntheses). Provide the FULL page body including the YAML frontmatter. The response includes a `dangling` list — any [[wikilink]] in the body you just wrote that doesn't resolve to an existing page in any domain. Each entry is either a target you should write next (offer the author a stub) or a slug typo / speculative reference that should be pruned (offer the author the prune). Resolve before moving on so the link graph stays clean. It also includes `schema_violations` -- every way the page breaks the domain's page schema (missing frontmatter `type`, missing required frontmatter keys, missing required `## ` sections, type/domain not matching the path). The page IS written either way; if the list is non-empty, rewrite the page to fix every entry before moving on. `schema_checked: false` means no schema was available, not that the page is clean.

body.description: Full page content including YAML frontmatter at the top.

type.description: Page type directory: entities, concepts, sources, or syntheses.

tor-character-mcp.name: tor_calling_template
tor-character-mcp.description: Return the full template for one Calling: name, description, body text, the 2 added Favoured Skills, and the Shadow Path that this Calling steers the hero's corruption toward.

tor-character-mcp.name: tor_create_starting_hero
tor-character-mcp.description: Build a fully-resolved TOR 2e starting hero from player elections. Validates that the chosen Distinctive Features are offered by the culture, that Favoured Skill allocations sum to exactly 10 and only target Favoured Skills (culture's 6 + calling's 2), that the Combat Proficiency primary is one of the culture's options, and that no skill exceeds rank 6. Returns the hero as structured JSON in `hero` plus a `formatted` field rendered per the `format` arg (defaults to markdown for chat). Use this instead of asking the LLM to compose a character — the LLM cannot get the rules right consistently. Workflow: call tor_culture_template first to read each skill's base rank, then plan an allocation where base+alloc never exceeds 6. The LLM's job is to talk to the player about the elections; THIS TOOL builds the sheet. Reply to the player by paraphrasing the `hero` JSON in your own words — the `formatted` field is a convenience for direct rendering and need not be copied verbatim.

attribute_row.description: Row 1-6 from the culture's attribute table.

blessing_attribute.description: Strength|Heart|Wits when culture's blessing is player-choice.

combat_primary.description: One of the culture's primary combat-proficiency choices.

combat_secondary.description: Player's choice of any other combat proficiency.

distinctive_features.description: Exactly 2 features from the culture's offered list (verbatim, case-sensitive — copy from tor_culture_template.distinctive_features).

favoured_skill_allocations.description: Map of skill name → extra ranks. Keys are the canonical UPPERCASE skill names (AWE, ENHEARTEN, PERSUADE, ATHLETICS, TRAVEL, STEALTH, AWARENESS, INSIGHT, SCAN, HUNTING, HEALING, EXPLORE, SONG, COURTESY, RIDDLE, CRAFT, BATTLE, LORE) but the server is case-insensitive. Only Favoured Skills (culture's 6 + calling's 2) may receive points. Must sum to exactly 10. Each final rank (culture base + alloc) capped at 6 — read tor_culture_template.skill_base_ranks before allocating.

format.description: Rendering style for the optional `formatted` field. Default is "markdown" — produces a clean character sheet that renders well in OWUI chat. "plain" drops markup for terminals/logs. "none" omits the formatted field entirely (structured `hero` JSON is always returned).

tor-character-mcp.name: tor_culture_template
tor-character-mcp.description: Return the canonical starting block for one Heroic Culture: 6-row attribute table, 18-skill base ranks, Favoured Skill list, Combat Proficiency options, Distinctive Features, languages, Standard of Living, sample names, and cultural notes (e.g. 'Beset by Woe' for Elves). Values are verbatim from the rulebooks.

tor-character-mcp.name: tor_list_callings
tor-character-mcp.description: List the six TOR 2e Callings (Captain, Champion, Messenger, Scholar, Treasure-Hunter, Warden). Each Calling adds 2 Favoured Skills on top of the culture's six and assigns the hero's Shadow Path.

tor-character-mcp.name: tor_list_cultures
tor-character-mcp.description: List the Heroic Cultures available for TOR 2e character creation. Returns slug + display name + source rulebook for each. Use the slug as the `culture` argument to other tools.

sweep-mcp.name: run_sweep
sweep-mcp.description: Trigger a model-testing sweep against the homelab ARC runner. Forwards to the n8n model-sweep-kickoff webhook, which dispatches the GHA workflow and files a tracking GitHub issue. Returns immediately with sweep_id + issue_url; the sweep itself runs for 5-90 minutes depending on the payload set. The tracking issue gets dual-summarize comments (local LLM + Claude) when the sweep completes. Single-sweep mutex enforced server-side: a second call while a sweep is in flight returns an error pointing at the in-flight run.

model.description: The ollama model tag to sweep (e.g. 'qwen3.6:35b', 'devstral:24b'). Must exist on the cluster's ollama service.

payload.description: Which benchmark payload(s) to run. 'all' (default) runs every payload (~1-2 hours); a single name like 'instruction_following' runs just that one (~5-15 min). Names match files in benchmarks/payloads/ in the model-testing repo.

requester.description: Free-form identifier for who/what asked. Surfaces in the tracking issue title. Default 'mcp:unknown'. LLMs should fill this in with something distinguishable, e.g. 'mcp:chat-session-2026-06-01'.

runs.description: Number of runs per (model, payload) pair. Default '1'. Higher values average out noise but multiply runtime.

tinysearch-mcp.name: get_current_datetime
tinysearch-mcp.description: Return the current date and time in UTC. Call this first for time-sensitive questions, relative dates such as latest, this year, or last month, or before adding year/month/day context to a search query.

tinysearch-mcp.name: search
tinysearch-mcp.description: Fast discovery for one to five independent items. Use one item for a simple lookup, multiple only for independent subquestions, and domains for hard source restrictions. Does not crawl or rerank.

items.description: One to five items, each with query and optional positive domains.
items.title: Items

domains.description: Deprecated; positive domains for the single-query compatibility form.
domains.title: Domains

tinysearch-mcp.name: scrape_urls
tinysearch-mcp.description: Inspect one to five URL/query pairs. Each item has url and optional query; omit query or use '*' for page-order content, or provide a focused query describing needed evidence. Related links are navigation candidates; batch URLs only after selecting them. Returns each item's success or error independently.

items.description: One to five items, each with url and optional query.
items.title: Items

tinysearch-mcp.name: browser_navigate
tinysearch-mcp.description: Open an exact URL in a live browser and return a view of the page. Call scrape_urls on this exact URL first -- most pages, including ordinary articles, are static, and scrape_urls reads them for a fraction of the cost of a browser. Reach for this tool only when that call actually came back thin, empty, or clearly incomplete, or the page needs a read-only interaction first (a cookie banner, a "load more" control, content that renders after load, a client-side search box) to reveal what was asked for. Not a discovery tool. find narrows what comes back to the matching nodes and their context, not the whole tree. Pass it unless you truly need the tree: a full page can be 50x larger. Then drive the same page with browser_act.

find.description: Regex (case-insensitive) to return instead of the tree, e.g. 'click|submit'. Plain text that is not valid regex is matched as a literal substring, so ordinary words need no escaping.
find.title: Find

depth.description: Unfiltered view only: max tree depth. 0 = configured default.
depth.title: Depth

tinysearch-mcp.name: browser_act
tinysearch-mcp.description: One action on the page browser_navigate opened. look() reads it without touching it. click(target) / type(target, text, submit) act on a ref you saw in a returned view; never invent a ref or selector, never type credentials. wait_for(time | text | text_gone). tabs(tab_action, index). close() when done. All but close return a page view, so find narrows what comes back to the matching nodes and their context, not the whole tree. Pass it unless you truly need the tree: a full page can be 50x larger. Read-only steps revealing already-public content (pagination, expanding a section, a cookie banner) need no confirmation; real-world side effects do.

text.description: type: text to enter. wait_for: text to await.
